units.text: ⟦0⟧18.1.2 Handling Changes to the Directory Structure⟦1⟧
units.sourceHTML: 18.1.2 Handling Changes to the Directory Structure

units.text: ⟦0⟧ and ⟦1⟧ do not handle some changes to directory structure. For example, suppose one directory tree contains a directory named ‘⟦2⟧’ with some subsidiary files, and another contains a file with the same name ‘⟦3⟧’. ‘⟦4⟧’ does not output enough information for ⟦5⟧ to transform the directory subtree into the file.
units.sourceHTML: diff and patch do not handle some changes to directory structure. For example, suppose one directory tree contains a directory named ‘D’ with some subsidiary files, and another contains a file with the same name ‘D’. ‘diff -r’ does not output enough information for patch to transform the directory subtree into the file.

units.text: There should be a way to specify that a file has been removed without having to include its entire contents in the patch file. There should also be a way to tell ⟦0⟧ that a file was renamed, even if there is no way for ⟦1⟧ to generate such information. There should be a way to tell ⟦2⟧ that a file’s timestamp has changed, even if its contents have not changed.
units.sourceHTML: There should be a way to specify that a file has been removed without having to include its entire contents in the patch file. There should also be a way to tell patch that a file was renamed, even if there is no way for diff to generate such information. There should be a way to tell patch that a file’s timestamp has changed, even if its contents have not changed.

units.text: These problems can be fixed by extending the ⟦0⟧ output format to represent changes in directory structure, and extending ⟦1⟧ to understand these extensions.
units.sourceHTML: These problems can be fixed by extending the diff output format to represent changes in directory structure, and extending patch to understand these extensions.
